problem_statement: We're comparing the models to rank applications by their risk of a default event occuring within 90 days after the application

notes.evidence: The XGBoost model scored the highest at 0.3338 at the average percision metric which is the metric we are concerned with as the default occuring is a rarity, and that's the metric that catches it, while the logsitic regression was teh fastest and scored the highest in the ROC metric
notes.limitation: The random split does not show us how accurately the model will perform on future applicants
notes.next_test: Perform a differnt split and check whether the models will perform the same way.

exit_answers: Because AP catches rare of uncommon events and defaults are rare events
Because we need the model to accurately choose the number of trees and not tune it based on the set and make the scores untrustworthy
